Load All Element-UI Dependencies

Source: R/el_dependencies.R
use_element.Rd

Convenience function to load Vue, Element-UI, and layout CSS dependencies. Use this when you want to use Element-UI components in non-el_page layouts (e.g., bslib::page_sidebar, shiny::navbarPage).

Usage

use_element(
  theme = el_layout_css_dependency(),
  offline = TRUE,
  dev = getOption("shiny.element.dev", FALSE),
  locale = getOption("shiny.element.locale", "en"),
  size = NULL,
  z_index = NULL,
  colors = NULL
)

Arguments

theme

CSS dependency function or list (optional, default is el_layout_css_dependency())

offline

Serve Element UI from the copy bundled with this package rather than the unpkg CDN. See element_ui_dependency().

dev

Load the development build of Vue instead of vue.min.js, so Vue's warnings are not stripped. Defaults to getOption("shiny.element.dev", FALSE).

locale

Language for Element UI's built-in text. English by default, or getOption("shiny.element.locale") when set. See el_locale_dependency().

size, z_index

Element's global config, as Vue.use(Element, {size, zIndex}) sets it: the size of every component not given one of its own ("medium", "small" or "mini"), and the z-index its popups start from (2000 by default). NULL leaves Element's default.

colors

Element's primary, success, warning and danger, as a named list – or a bslib::bs_theme() to take them from, such as the page's own. Element's components are recoloured with them, tints and shades included, as Element's theme picker does. el_page() takes them from its theme.

Value

A list of htmlDependency objects

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(bslib)
ui <- page_sidebar(
  use_element(),
  el_button("btn1", "Click me")
)
} # }
